tasks.short: Compile scripts, program notes and other production material.

steps.what: List the scripts and program notes for this production
Draft scene lines from each script and program note

loop.input: The scripts and program notes the producer marked in scope
loop.output: One scene line with character, place and prop for each scene
loop.check: The line names a scene the script contains, and the character, place and prop appear in that scene or the program note. A line that adds a person or place is rejected.
loop.stop: Stop when every scene in the named scripts has one line or is marked missing. The producer rewrites a rejected line. One pass per scene.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scripts and program notes are free text, so a fixed field map cannot read a scene.

steps.what: Confirm each scene line matches the script and notes
Walk the crew through the compiled production material

tasks.design: The producer marks which scripts and program notes in the {DOCS} store belong to this production. A bounded loop drafts one scene line per scene and stops when she has confirmed every scene or marked it missing. She still walks the crew through the accepted lines. Nothing is sent outside the company.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scripts and program notes are free text, so a fixed form could not pull a scene, a character or a prop.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can propose one scene line and stop when the producer confirms that scene. A production tool already drafts a script breakdown for a person to check.
tasks.still_hard: She still decides which material belongs to the production. Handwritten notes, and scripts whose rightholder has reserved mining, still need her own reading.
tasks.human_edge: Only she knows which note is in this production and which scene the crew must not treat as settled.

ambition.what: Confirm which scenes are ready on each new script draft during the week, not only on the locked draft.

tasks.altitude: She spends the old reading time on the scene lines the draft got wrong, and she still decides what the crew may treat as the pack.

reach.task: Cut the picture from the confirmed scene lines
reach.learn: Which scenes the producer marked missing, so the cut does not invent coverage.

evidence.claim: Yamdu drafts a script breakdown from a script. That breakdown has been in beta since October 2025. The same product also keeps call sheets, schedules and budgets.
Text and data mining is allowed unless the rightholder reserves it, online by machine-readable means. The digest names the Dutch statute as the national example; other countries differ.
In a mid-size company the producer compiles scripts and program notes into a pack and walks the crew through it. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The focal role is the producer. Before any draft she records production title, file name and whether the file is in scope. If a file cannot be read she types the scene line herself.
The document store already holds the scripts. Opening a stored file is existing runtime and is not extra human time.
Four hours per 100 baseline hours is her time to keep the scene, character, place and prop headings aligned with how this company writes scripts. That upkeep is her work.
The crew walk stays inside the company. This task does not publish the pack.
unknowns: Whether these rightholders have reserved text and data mining.
Whether program notes name private people.
Which store holds the scripts today.
research_questions: How often does a script change after the first scene pass?
What share of program notes arrives as a file rather than talk?

already_counted.description: She still confirms every scene line. That review stays in s3 and is not deducted again.

incremental.description: The producer keeps the scene, character, place and prop headings aligned with how this company writes scripts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Clean digital scripts confirm quickly. Handwritten program notes, or a script the loop may not read, put more lines back on her, so the saving stays inside this band.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Resolve a personnel problem between people on the production.

steps.what: Hear each account of the personnel problem
Decide what the production can change for these parties
Tell the dissenting parties the production change

tasks.design: The producer hears each person, decides what the production can change, and tells the parties herself. No tool drafts the settlement or speaks for her. The conversation stays in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: The hard part is what these people will accept. There is no rule that turns two accounts into a settlement.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the hearing or the talk. The lack of a paperwork step is why no build is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, tone and what the production can actually change stay with her. A wrong word can harm the people involved.
tasks.human_edge: The parties need her to hear both sides and to say what will change. A draft must not settle a people dispute.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in her week. She still hears both sides and tells them the outcome herself.

reach.task: Hear a performer who will not work with a colleague
reach.learn: Which production change the producer already told the parties, so the talent talk does not reopen it.

evidence.claim: A producer on a mid-size production hears a personnel dispute in person and tells the parties what will change. Model knowledge. No product in the digest does this liaison.

assumptions: The focal role is the producer. The parties are people on this production, and the exposure prior is the team, so the talk is inside the company and is not a versioned send.
No structured record is required for the settlement. She does not open a new personnel file in this task.
Upkeep is zero because no heading list, mapping or tool is added. The prior that some of this task vanishes is not used, because no step has a mechanism that shortens it.
unknowns: Whether a party is a freelancer outside the company.
Whether the dispute includes health information.
Whether national rules require a written note of the settlement.
research_questions: How often is one meeting enough to close a personnel problem on this production?

already_counted.description: Telling the parties the change stays in full in s3. That time is not deducted again.

incremental.description: No new heading list or mapping. The liaison stays a conversation, so ongoing upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The design does not shorten the hearing, the decision or the talk, so no time comes back.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate writers, directors, managers and other production personnel.

steps.what: Meet writers, directors and managers about the production
Write the next activities of writers, directors and managers
Draft the call schedule from those activities
Check the schedule covers the writers and directors
Send the accepted schedule to the production personnel

tasks.design: She meets the writers, directors and managers, then enters each next activity in the {PROJECT} tool. That tool fills a call schedule from person, day, place and activity, using its own schedule feature before any custom code. She checks the schedule, and only then does {EMAIL} send that accepted version. The meeting stays hers.
tasks.previous_blocker: The day's commitments were spoken, then copied by hand into a mail. The project tool was not given person, day, place and activity as fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she has entered those fields, a project tool can fill a call schedule. Production tools already keep schedules of this kind.
tasks.still_hard: People change their promise in the room. She still decides which activity is real before anything is sent.
tasks.human_edge: She is the one who can tell a real commitment from a hope, and who may allow the schedule to leave the company.

ambition.what: See, before the steering meeting, which writer, director or manager has no next activity, and settle that gap in the meeting.

tasks.altitude: She still runs the steering meeting. Less of the week goes to copying a schedule into mail, and she still decides whether that schedule may go out.

reach.task: Set the technical crew to the day's work
reach.learn: Which call schedule the producer accepted, so the crew is not given a second plan.

evidence.claim: Yamdu keeps call sheets, schedules and budgets, and drafts a script breakdown. The schedule claim is the part used here.
Producers pass the day's plan to writers, directors and managers by mail after a meeting. Model knowledge, consistent with call sheets travelling by mail.

assumptions: The focal role is the producer. She produces the activity notes: person, day, place and activity. If the project tool lacks a field she types it. The schedule fill is tried first as configuration of that tool.
Writers and hired directors are often outside the company, so the meeting is with outside parties and the schedule mail leaves the company. The meeting is not a versioned send.
Three hours per 100 baseline hours is her time to keep person, day, place and activity headings matched to how this production names them. Existing mail delivery is not human effort.
A change to the schedule after she accepts it voids the send approval.
unknowns: Whether this company's writers and directors are employees, in which case the mail would stay inside.
Whether a project tool is already in use, or the schedule still lives only in documents.
Who else must agree a schedule that names overtime or a location change.
research_questions: What share of call schedules is rewritten after the steering meeting?
Do external writers receive the schedule by mail today?

already_counted.description: Checking the schedule against what people agreed stays in s4 and is not deducted again.

incremental.description: The producer keeps the person, day, place and activity headings matched to how this production names them.

approvals.approved_version: Call schedule as the producer accepted it for this production day

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the meeting rewrites the day, she rebuilds the notes before any send, so only the final send comes back. When the notes are already complete, the fill and the send both come back.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Obtain rights to scripts or to existing video footage.

steps.what: List scripts and existing footage that need rights
Read grants already held for those scripts and footage
Decide the use and term for the rights ask
Write the rights request for that script or footage
Send the accepted rights request for that footage
Meet the rightholder about rights the request left open

tasks.design: The producer lists the scripts and footage, reads the grants already held, and writes the rights request herself. {EMAIL} sends only the text she wrote, after that text is the accepted version. Terms the mail cannot close stay in her meeting with the rightholder. No tool decides that a script or footage is cleared.
tasks.previous_blocker: The request is a legal ask with a high cost if the use, the term or the footage is wrong. A form could not judge an existing grant.
tasks.enabler_now: The mail she already writes can leave through the mailbox once she has settled the text. The judgement of the grant stays manual.
tasks.still_hard: Reading a grant, setting the use and the term, and negotiating with the rightholder stay with her. A wrong clearance is a legal and financial loss.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can decide the use, the term and the fee limit, and only she can tell a rightholder what the production will accept.
tasks.altitude: She still reads the grants and still agrees every ask. The week loses only the act of sending a request she has already written.

reach.task: Use existing footage in a shot
reach.learn: Which footage the producer has not cleared, so the shot is not built on it.

evidence.claim: A producer asks the rightholder, by mail and in a meeting, before the production uses a script or existing footage. Model knowledge. The digest does not name a product that obtains those rights.
A tool that reads a script can be blocked where the rightholder has reserved text and data mining. That reservation is not itself a grant to use the script or the footage in the production.

assumptions: The focal role is the producer. She produces the rights needed list (title and whether it is a script or footage) and the ask terms (use, term, fee limit). She writes the request text herself. Fallback: she sends the mail by hand if the mailbox cannot send the accepted text.
Contracts sit in the document store. This design does not add a contract system. Sending the accepted text is configuration of the mailbox she already uses.
Three hours per 100 baseline hours is her time to keep title, use, term, fee limit and rightholder headings current. That upkeep is her work.
The rightholder is outside the company. The meeting is a talk, not a second send. A change to the request text voids the send approval.
unknowns: Who at the company may bind a fee, besides the producer.
Whether grants already live in a contract store.
Which footage items have a rightholder the company can already name.
research_questions: What share of rights asks is closed by mail, and what share needs the meeting?
How often does the request text change after she first writes it?

already_counted.description: Writing the rights request stays in full in s4. That time is the human acceptance of the text and is not deducted again.

incremental.description: The producer keeps title, use, term, fee limit and rightholder headings current for each open ask.

approvals.approved_version: Rights request text as the producer left it for this title, use and term

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the rightholder will only talk, the mail is a small slice. When a clear request is what she sends, most of that send comes back and the meeting still stays.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still settles personnel problems herself, still agrees every rights ask, and still runs the steering meeting. The week shifts from typing scene lines, and from copying a call schedule into mail, toward confirming those artefacts. She does not gain a right to publish the production or to treat footage as cleared.
reach: Film and Video Editors: cut only scenes the producer confirmed, and learn which scenes were marked missing.
Media Technical Directors/Managers: staff the day from the accepted call schedule, and learn which activities were still blank.
Special Effects Artists and Animators: do not build a shot on footage the producer has not cleared.
skills_to_grow: Confirm a scene line against the script and the program note, including a line the draft got wrong.
Enter person, day, place and activity before a call schedule is filled.
State a rights ask as use, term and fee limit before any mail goes to a rightholder.
role.ambitious_version: She briefs a second unit from a confirmed scene pack the same day a draft arrives, and she opens the steering meeting already knowing which writer has no next activity. She still chooses who is cast, and she still agrees every rights ask before it goes to a rightholder. She does not publish the production.
